name: Cyrillic (Russian)
signature: Latin-like at a glance, but studded with give-aways: Я, Ж, Д, Б, и.
combination: A true alphabet: letters are written left-to-right in a row and each spells a sound. No inherent vowels, no diacritics in normal text (stress is unmarked). Two letters — ъ (hard sign) and ь (soft sign) — spell no sound of their own; they modify the consonant before them.
notes: The 33 lowercase Russian letters. complete:false because the UPPERCASE forms are not yet in the inventory (lessons use the lowercase citation form); the lowercase set itself is whole. Several letters are 'false friends' that look like Latin letters but sound different — those are flagged. Descended from Greek (via Old Church Slavonic), so many letters are Greek cousins: С↔sigma, Р↔rho, П↔pi, Ф↔phi.

components: a rounded body entered through the upper shoulder
strokeOrder: start at the upper-left shoulder, sweep up and right, descend into the body, then circle counterclockwise around the lower bowl to its right junction without lifting
continue down the right-hand finishing stem in the same pen-down run
letters.strokeOrderNote: verified one-stroke isolated school-hand teaching form fitted to the bundled printed outline

strokeOrderSource.citation: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase а demonstration, 00:50–00:55, YouTube, 5 February 2013
strokeOrderSource.variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 00:50–00:55 lowercase а demonstration, the rounded body and right-hand finishing stem are written in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated handwritten а is a round single-storey form; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a double-storey printed form with an extra upper shoulder. This learner path preserves the source's one-run body-to-stem motion while fitting that shoulder as the entry into the lower loop. Connected cursive may add entry and exit joins, and individual handwriting may round or slant the body differently.

letters.notes: Looks and sounds like Latin a.

components: a joined rising shoulder and top flag
strokeOrder: begin at the body's upper-right junction and circle counterclockwise around the lower body back to that junction without lifting
continue through the rising shoulder and sweep the top flag right in the same pen-down run
letters.strokeOrderNote: verified one-stroke isolated school-hand teaching form fitted to the bundled printed outline

strokeOrderSource.citation: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase б demonstration, 01:13–01:18, YouTube, 5 February 2013
strokeOrderSource.variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 01:13–01:18 lowercase б demonstration, the pen circles the lower body counterclockwise, closes it at the upper-right junction, and continues through the rising shoulder into the rightward top flag in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand crosses diagonally from the body's upper-right junction toward the rising shoulder; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph joins its ascender through the body's upper-left shoulder instead. This learner path preserves the source's uninterrupted body-to-flag order while routing that transition along the printed upper shoulder so it remains on the font's ink. Connected cursive may lengthen the top flag into an exit join, and individual handwriting may narrow, round, or slant the lower body differently.

strokeOrder: begin at the baseline, climb through the tall upper loop, and descend the left stem back to the baseline without lifting
continue right from the baseline and circle counterclockwise around the rounded lower bowl in the same pen-down run
letters.strokeOrderNote: verified one-stroke isolated school-hand teaching form fitted to the bundled printed outline

strokeOrderSource.citation: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase в demonstration, 01:33–01:38, YouTube, 5 February 2013
strokeOrderSource.variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 01:33–01:38 lowercase в demonstration, the pen starts at the baseline, climbs through the tall upper loop, descends to the baseline, and continues counterclockwise around the rounded lower bowl in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand resembles a looped Latin cursive b with one tall ascender loop above a lower bowl; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a compact printed form with two stacked bowls attached to a straight left stem. This learner path preserves the source's baseline-to-upper-loop-to-baseline-to-lower-bowl order while routing the ascender through the printed upper bowl and left stem so it remains on the font's ink. Connected cursive may add entry and exit joins, and individual handwriting may narrow, round, or slant either loop differently.

strokeOrder: begin at the baseline, climb the upright stem, and sweep right along the top bar without lifting
reverse along the top bar and descend the upright to the baseline in the same pen-down run
letters.strokeOrderNote: verified one-stroke school-hand lift count fitted to the bundled printed outline

strokeOrderSource.citation: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase г demonstration, 01:54–01:57, YouTube, 5 February 2013
strokeOrderSource.variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 01:54–01:57 lowercase г demonstration, the pen rises from the baseline into the main shoulder, descends and turns at the baseline, then continues through a smaller rising-and-falling exit arch in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand is a rounded cursive form with two humps; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a block-like printed form with one straight upright and a top bar, and has no exit arch. This learner path preserves the source's baseline-to-shoulder-to-baseline lift count while fitting the printed form: climb the upright, sweep right along the top bar, reverse to the junction, and descend the upright without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's smaller exit arch, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, or slant both humps differently.

components: a joined base shelf with two feet
strokeOrder: begin at the body's upper-right junction and circle counterclockwise around the closed body back to that junction without lifting
continue down the right stem, retrace the right foot, sweep left along the base shelf, retrace the left foot, and finish rightward along the shelf in the same pen-down run
letters.strokeOrderNote: verified one-stroke school-hand lift count fitted to the bundled printed outline

strokeOrderSource.citation: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase д demonstration, 02:14–02:19, YouTube, 5 February 2013
strokeOrderSource.variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 02:14–02:19 lowercase д demonstration, the pen circles the rounded body counterclockwise, closes it at the upper-right junction, descends below the baseline, loops left, and rises into the rightward exit in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand resembles a looped Latin cursive g; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a block-like printed form with a trapezoidal body, a joined base shelf, and two separated feet rather than one descender loop. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-descender order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed form: circle the body, descend through the right stem and foot, retrace to the shelf, sweep left, retrace the left foot, and finish rightward along the shelf without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's below-baseline loop and exit join, and individual handwriting may narrow, round, or slant the body and loop differently.
